content: Sulfadiazine should not be administered to infants under 2 months of age, except when used as an adjunctive therapy with pyrimethamine for the treatment of congenital toxoplasmosis. For infants over 2 months of age and children, the initial dose should be half of the calculated 24-hour dose. The maintenance dose is 150 mg per kilogram of body weight or 4 grams per square meter of body surface area, divided into 4 to 6 doses over a 24-hour period. The maximum allowable dose is 6 grams within a 24-hour timeframe. For the prevention of rheumatic fever, the dosage depends on the child’s weight. For children weighing less than 30 kilograms (66 pounds), the recommended dose is 500 milligrams every 24 hours. For children weighing more than 30 kilograms (66 pounds), the recommended dose is 1 gram every 24 hours. For adults, the initial dose ranges from 2 grams to 4 grams. The maintenance dose is also 2 grams to 4 grams, divided into 3 to 6 doses over a 24-hour period.
